$comment: This extension implements succession rules derived from Hindu law as codified in specific jurisdictions. The extension name references the legal tradition, not the personal religious beliefs of any individual. A person of any faith (or none) may be subject to these rules depending on their jurisdiction of domicile.
title: Hindu Succession Extension
description: Hindu succession law specifics: Mitakshara/Dayabhaga schools, HUF coparcenary, heir classifications under the Hindu Succession Act 1956, stridhan assets, agricultural land ceiling rules, and NRI complications.
dataProvenance: Hindu Succession Act 1956 (as amended 2005), Indian Succession Act 1925, Transfer of Property Act 1882

relationship.$comment: Should align with core kinshipType values (e.g. parent_child_biological for son/daughter, grandparent_grandchild for grandson). The 2005 Amendment to the Hindu Succession Act gives daughters equal coparcenary rights — coparceners are no longer limited to male descendants

heirClass.$comment: class_I: 16 heirs under the 2005 Amendment — spouse (relationship.json), children (parent_child_biological), mother, grandchildren through sons and daughters (grandparent_grandchild + lineage), great-grandchildren (chained parent_child), widow of predeceased son (derived from relationship + kinship chain). class_II: 9 entries — Entry V: father's father/mother (grandparent_grandchild + lineage: paternal). Entry VII: father's brother/sister (uncle_aunt + lineage: paternal = agnate). Entry VIII: mother's father/mother (grandparent_grandchild + lineage: maternal). Entry IX: mother's brother/sister (uncle_aunt + lineage: maternal = cognate). agnate: relatives traced wholly through males — every kinship hop has lineage: paternal. cognate: at least one female link in the chain — at least one hop has lineage: maternal. The agnate-before-cognate priority means uncle_aunt + lineage: paternal inherits before uncle_aunt + lineage: maternal.

scheduleEntry.description: The specific entry from the Hindu Succession Act Schedule that this heir falls under. More precise than heirClass alone — distinguishes e.g. 'son of predeceased daughter' from 'daughter of predeceased son' within Class I
examples: Class I, Entry 9: widow of a predeceased son
Class II, Entry VII: father's brother, father's sister

state.$comment: ISO 3166-2 Indian state code (e.g. IN-MH, IN-KA)

instrumentType.description: Type of probate instrument being sought or granted. India has three distinct instruments depending on whether the deceased left a will and the nature of the assets
instrumentType.$comment: probate: testate estates (deceased left a valid will). letters_of_administration: intestate estates (no will) — movable assets and debts only, does not cover immovable property. succession_certificate: establishes heir's right to specific movable assets (bank accounts, shares, insurance) — often used alongside or instead of probate.

probateAdvisable.description: Whether probate is advisable for this estate. Section 213 (mandatory probate in Mumbai/Kolkata/Chennai) was deleted by the Repealing and Amending Act 2025 (Presidential assent 20 Dec 2025). Probate is now optional everywhere in India but remains strongly advisable — banks and housing societies may still request it in practice

crossStateAssets.description: Whether the estate includes assets in Indian states other than the primary jurisdiction. Affects which state's agricultural land ceiling laws apply and may require multiple court filings

hufProperty.description: Whether the estate includes Hindu Undivided Family coparcenary property. HUF property has special succession rules under the Hindu Succession Act — the 2005 Amendment gave daughters equal coparcenary rights. Must be distinguished from self-acquired property
